title: "Causal Analysis in Public Health Management"

## Almaz had a baby in Tigray in 2015.

Her baby lived. A Health Extension Worker was in the room. So was a new road that had cut the trip to the nearest hospital from four hours to ninety minutes. So was a school year that had kept her in class until she was nineteen.

**Which of those things saved her baby?**

That question — which of the things happening at the same time actually mattered — is the question this course is about.

::: {.callout-note}
**A practical course on causal thinking for global health.** Designed for high school learners with no statistics or programming background. Built around real Maternal & Newborn Health stories from Ethiopia, Rwanda, Kenya, and Tanzania, using public data from WHO, UNICEF, DHS, and Lancet.
:::

## What you will need

Curiosity, and a willingness to sketch your ideas on paper. No math degree, no programming background. The R code on the companion pages is there to read first; you can run it later.
